t.1.214.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Dwelling in Indraprastha, they slew other kings at the command of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and of Śāṃtanava.
t.1.214.3: That bull among the Bharatas pursued dharma, kāma and artha equally, honoring them as a man rich in kinsmen honors three kinsmen who are his equals.
t.1.214.2: Taking refuge in the Dharmarāja, whose deeds bore the marks of virtue, the whole world lived in happiness, as embodied souls rest in their own bodies.
t.1.214.7: Accompanied by his four brothers, the king shone all the more brightly, like a great sacrifice spread out with the Vedas being employed in its performance.
t.1.214.8: But the foremost brahmins, Dhaumya and the others, equal to Bṛhaspati, surrounded him and attended upon him, as the immortals attend upon Prajāpati.
t.1.214.9: In Dharmarāja, as in the spotless full moon, the eyes and hearts of the subjects alike took delight with exceeding affection.
t.1.214.10: Yet the subjects did not rejoice merely through fate or through mere goodwill; whatever was pleasing to their minds, he brought about by his deeds.
t.1.214.4: Among them, dharma, artha and kāma, evenly apportioned as though embodied upon the earth, the king shone forth like a fourth.
t.1.214.11: For nothing improper, nothing untrue, nothing false, and nothing unpleasant was ever known to be spoken by the wise and sweet-spoken Pārtha.
t.1.214.12: For he, the most excellent of the Bharatas, of very great splendor, desiring to do what was beneficial for the whole world and for himself as well, took delight in his rule.
t.1.214.6: Through that ruler of the earth, Fortune found a firm abode, wisdom a sure refuge, and the whole of dharma a kinsman.
t.1.214.5: In that lord of the people the Vedas found a supreme student, the great sacrifices a performer, and the social classes a virtuous protector.
t.1.214.13: Thus all the Pāṇḍavas dwelt there joyful, their fever of anxiety gone, making the kings of the earth tremble with their own splendor.
t.1.214.15: Surrounded by our friends, O Madhusūdana, we shall amuse ourselves there and return again in the evening; let this please you, O Janārdana.
t.1.214.17: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having bid farewell to the Dharmarāja and taken his leave, O Bhārata, Pārtha and Govinda then departed, surrounded by their friends.
t.1.214.14: Then, after a few days, Bībhatsu said to Kṛṣṇa: "Kṛṣṇa, the hot days are upon us; let us go to the Yamunā."
t.1.214.18: Having reached an excellent pleasure-ground, abounding in many kinds of trees and furnished with buildings both lofty and low, resembling the abode of Puraṃdara,
t.1.214.16: O son of Kuntī, this pleases me too: that we, surrounded by our friends, should sport in the water as we please, Pārtha.
t.1.214.19: They came to a spot furnished with savoury, costly foods, both hard and soft, and with drinks, and with garlands of many kinds, a spot fit for Vārṣṇeya and Pārtha.
t.1.214.21: Some of the women of Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha sported in the forest, some in the water, and some in the houses, each as the place allowed and as pleased her.
t.1.214.20: The two of them entered the place, which was filled with lovely jewels of every kind, and all the people sported there as each pleased, O Bhārata.
t.1.214.23: Some of the women, delighted, danced, while others shouted aloud; still others laughed, and others drank the finest liquor.
t.1.214.22: Draupadī and Subhadrā, in the height of their intoxication, would bestow costly garments and ornaments upon the women.
t.1.214.24: Some women there wept, and they struck one another; and others whispered secrets to one another.
t.1.214.25: That richly prosperous forest was filled on every side with the sound of flutes, vīṇās, and mṛdaṅga drums, all delightful to the mind.
t.1.214.26: While that festivity was thus going on, the two delights of the Kurus and the Dāśārhas went to a certain very charming spot close by.
t.1.214.27: Having gone there, O king, the two great-souled Kṛṣṇas, conquerors of enemy cities, then sat down upon two very costly seats.
t.1.214.28: There the two, Pārtha and Mādhava, took their pleasure, recounting to each other many deeds of valour and many delights from times long past.
t.1.214.29: Then a brahmin approached Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya as they sat there joyfully, like the two Aśvins on the vault of heaven.
t.1.214.31: He was like the newly risen sun, clad in black garments and wearing matted locks, his face like a lotus petal, tawny-hued, as though blazing with fiery splendor.
t.1.214.30: He was like a great śāla tree and shone like molten gold, tawny-yellow, with a tawny beard, his height matching his breadth.
t.1.214.32: When that radiant best of the twice-born had come up to them, the two Kṛṣṇas, Arjuna and Vāsudeva, swiftly sprang up and stood before him.
